finding.detail: Cached/batched authentication paths can return an active user before fallback-only non-API token idle enforcement. Existing synthetic1.1 evidence demonstrates batched acceptance and nonbatched refusal; full HTTP pipeline remains to be proved.

actualGatewaySettingsReadOnly.method: Instantiate actual config under captured actual gunicorn process environment, exposing only selected non-secret settings. No DB/JWT/network mutation.

providerSettings.limitation: Provider processes do not use the selected gunicorn predicate; failed probes establish no settings conclusion.

minimalNextStep: Use existing public AUTH_CACHE_ENABLED=false and AUTH_CACHE_BATCH_QUERIES=false together as an isolated candidate mitigation; disabling batching alone leaves cache early return.

Prove full real HTTP auth pipeline with synthetic inactive session token, API-token exemption, ordinary expiry/signature/revocation, fresh activity and disabled user. Bind actual per-role settings before activation.

If retaining caches is necessary, factor the existing idle enforcement into one shared auth gate before every successful user return; preserve API exemption and activity/revocation semantics, without copying auth route logic into another platform.
fallbackLimits: Old1.0.8 carries the same idle path, so it cannot be claimed as a stronger universal fallback.
New session_start/original-iat refresh and predecessor revocation, single-winner refresh and max-lifetime on refresh require explicit backward compatibility or refusal.
Personal-team and lost-membership permission behavior differs; schema compatibility alone cannot authorize downgrade.
